title: Normal launch awaits startLiveServices() (bridge init + notification-plugin init + ~25 listener/retrier starts) BEFORE runApp — share-launch already proves it's deferrable
userSymptom: App shows a black/splash screen noticeably longer on every cold open; first frame is delayed until Firebase + the notification plugin + all message/group/post listeners have initialized. Feels like a slow, heavy launch.
location: lib/main.dart:3017-3082 (startLiveServices defined), :3080-3082 (awaited on normal launch), :3090 (runApp), :3171 (deferredRuntimeStartup: isShareLaunch ? startLiveServices : null), :3549-3567 (deferral wiring); lib/core/notifications/flutter_notification_service.dart:23-44 (3 awaited platform calls)
evidence: if (!isShareLaunch) { await startLiveServices(); }  // main.dart:3080-3082, runs BEFORE runApp at :3090. startLiveServices() awaits ensureFirebaseReady(), bridge.initialize(), notificationService.initialize() then synchronously calls messageRouter.start()/chatMessageListener.start()/postListener.start()/...+~25 .start() calls. For share-launch the SAME function is passed as deferredRuntimeStartup (:3171) and run lazily post-frame via _ensureRuntimeServicesReady (:3560-3564) — so deferral is already implemented and safe.
rootCause: The runtime service bring-up (FCM, local-notifications plugin init = 3 awaited MethodChannel round-trips, plus all stream listeners/retriers) is on the synchronous pre-runApp critical path for the common (non-share) launch. None of it is needed to paint the first frame or the splash/StartupRouter; the node itself isn't even started here (that happens post-frame in StartupRouter._doStartP2P).
recommendation: Always pass startLiveServices as deferredRuntimeStartup (drop the isShareLaunch special-case) and remove the `await startLiveServices()` at :3081, OR wrap it in unawaited(...) / schedule via WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback so runApp() paints first and listeners come up immediately after the first frame. Incoming-message correctness is preserved because StartupRouter already calls ensureRuntimeServicesReady()/_ensureRuntimeServicesReady before routing and before _doStartP2P (:428, :629). notificationService.initialize() (launch-details + channel) can also move post-frame; only the initial-notification-open path needs it, which is already gated behind _handleInitialLocalNotificationLaunchWhenReady.

verdict.correctedLocation: lib/main.dart:3080-3082 (await startLiveServices on non-share launch), :3090 (runApp), :3171 (deferredRuntimeStartup: isShareLaunch ? startLiveServices : null), :3549-3567 (_ensureRuntimeServicesReady), :388-390 (separate awaited ensureFirebaseReady, NOT covered by the finding); lib/core/notifications/flutter_notification_service.dart:39,43,44 (3 awaited MethodChannel calls); lib/core/bridge/go_bridge_client.dart:158-184 (bridge.initialize — cheap); lib/features/identity/presentation/startup_router.dart:626-635 (_doStartP2P awaits ensureRuntimeServicesReady at :629 BEFORE startP2PNode at :635)
verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED structurally, but the finding overstates magnitude. The code is exactly as cited: main.dart:3080-3082 `if (!isShareLaunch) { await startLiveServices(); }` runs before runApp at :3090; startLiveServices (defined :3017-3078) awaits ensureFirebaseReady(), bridge.initialize(), notificationService.initialize() then synchronously fires ~25 .start() calls and ends marking 'runtime_services_ready' (:3077). Share-launch passes the SAME fn as deferredRuntimeStartup (:3171), run lazily by _ensureRuntimeServicesReady (:3549-3567) — deferral is already implemented. SAFETY CONFIRMED: StartupRouter is wired with ensureRuntimeServicesReady: _ensureRuntimeServicesReady (main.dart:4596), and _doStartP2P (startup_router.dart:626) does `await ensureRuntimeServicesReady()` (:629) BEFORE startP2PNode (:635); notification-open paths also await it (main.dart:3661,:3772; preSendReady at startup_router.dart:419/:1018). So deferring on normal launch would not let the node start or a notif route before listeners are up. HOWEVER, two magnitude corrections lower this from high to medium: (1) bridge.initialize() at go_bridge_client.dart:158-184 is CHEAP — it only subscribes to an EventChannel broadcast stream and sets _initialized=true; no platform round-trip, no Go runtime load (that is node:start, done later in startP2PNode). The finding's 'heavy bridge init' framing is inaccurate. (2) ensureFirebaseReady() is ALSO awaited INDEPENDENTLY at main.dart:388-390 on the non-share path, before startLiveServices; it is latched idempotent (firebaseInitialized at :356-360). So removing only the `await startLiveServices()` (per the recommendation) would NOT take Firebase off the pre-runApp critical path — Firebase init stays awaited at :389 regardless. The recommendation omits this. The genuinely deferrable awaited cost is therefore mainly notificationService.initialize() = 3 awaited MethodChannel round-trips (flutter_notification_service.dart:39 plugin.initialize, :43 ensureMknoonNotificationChannel, :44 getNotificationAppLaunchDetails) plus the time to run ~25 synchronous .start() calls. Those .start() calls are lightweight: e.g. PendingMessageRetrier holds StreamSubscription/Timer fields (pending_message_retrier.dart:77-80) and just registers listeners/timers, not blocking work. Net: real but modest per-cold-launch delay (a few MethodChannel hops + listener wiring), not the full Firebase+heavy-bridge stall implied.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Sound and safe to defer startLiveServices on normal launch — drop the isShareLaunch special-case so deferredRuntimeStartup is always startLiveServices and remove the `await startLiveServices()` at main.dart:3081 (or wrap in addPostFrameCallback). Correctness is preserved because StartupRouter._doStartP2P already awaits ensureRuntimeServicesReady() (startup_router.dart:629) before startP2PNode (:635), and notif-open/share-send paths await _ensureRuntimeServicesReady (main.dart:3661,:3772; preSendReady :419/:1018) before routing/sending. BUT to get the Firebase portion off the critical path you must ALSO defer or move the separate `await ensureFirebaseReady()` at main.dart:388-390 (the finding's recommendation misses this; leaving it means Firebase still blocks first frame). The largest concrete saving is moving notificationService.initialize() (3 awaited MethodChannel round-trips) post-frame; that path is already gated behind _handleInitialLocalNotificationLaunchWhenReady (:3771-3773) which awaits readiness, so it is safe. Measure with the existing StartupTiming marks ('firebase_ready', 'bridge_initialized', 'notification_service_ready', 'runtime_services_ready' vs 'run_app_called') before/after to confirm the actual first-frame win, since bridge.initialize is already cheap.

title: scrubLegacyGroupSecretsToSecureStorage has NO sentinel — runs two full encrypted-table scans on EVERY cold start, awaited before runApp
userSymptom: Cold start gets progressively slower the more media/group keys the user accumulates; on a busy account every launch pays a SQLCipher scan + row materialization cost on the main isolate before the UI appears.
location: lib/main.dart:835-838 (awaited, every launch); lib/core/secure_storage/legacy_group_secret_storage_scrub.dart:7-31 (no fast-exit), :41-45 + :80-84 (the two WHERE-NOT-NULL scans)
evidence: main.dart:835 `await scrubLegacyGroupSecretsToSecureStorage(db: db, secureKeyStore: secureKeyStore);` — unconditional, awaited before runApp. The function (scrub file:7) does NOT check a 'done' sentinel (contrast migrateSecretsToSecureStorage:23 which fast-exits on `containsKey(_kSecretsMigrated)`). It runs `db.query('media_attachments', where: "encryption_key_base64 IS NOT NULL AND encryption_key_base64 != ''")` (:41-45) and `db.query('group_keys', where: "encrypted_key IS NOT NULL AND encrypted_key != ''")` (:80-84). After the one-time migration these columns hold non-empty secureStoreReference strings, so the WHERE clauses STILL match every migrated row each launch — the query materializes all rows, then the loop skips them via isSecureStoreReference (:54, :95). Pure waste, scaling with media+group-key count, on the encrypted DB.
rootCause: A one-time backfill migration was left wired as an unconditional, sentinel-less, awaited startup step. The filter predicate matches already-migrated reference values, so the scan never shrinks.
recommendation: Add a one-shot sentinel exactly like migrateSecretsToSecureStorage: at function entry `if (await secureKeyStore.containsKey('legacy_group_secrets_scrubbed')) return;` and write it after a clean pass. Additionally tighten the WHERE clauses to exclude already-referenced rows (e.g. `AND encryption_key_base64 NOT LIKE 'secureref:%'`) so even a forced re-run is cheap. Either change makes it effectively free on the steady-state launch.

Prefix is 'secure:' per lib/core/secure_storage/secret_storage_references.dart:1-7.

The scrub (legacy_group_secret_storage_scrub.dart:7-31) has NO sentinel check, in direct contrast to migrate_secrets_to_secure_storage.dart:23 which fast-exits on containsKey(_kSecretsMigrated). It runs two encrypted-table scans: media_attachments WHERE "encryption_key_base64 IS NOT NULL AND encryption_key_base64 != ''" (:41-45) and group_keys WHERE "encrypted_key IS NOT NULL AND encrypted_key != ''" (:80-84). The existing test legacy_group_secret_storage_scrub_test.dart:111-147 asserts re-run is idempotent but never asserts a fast-exit, confirming re-scan is the intended (wasteful) steady-state behavior. So the core claim — sentinel-less, awaited, every-launch double-scan of an encrypted table that never shrinks — is true. I downgrade severity high->medium on MAGNITUDE: post-backfill the per-row loop does NO db.update / secureKeyStore.write (those only fire for un-migrated rows, which is zero steady-state); the residual cost is two index-less 2-column scans + SQLCipher page decryption + a Dart .startsWith per row. title: mirrorAllKeysToSecureStore + mirrorAllMutedGroups run serial nested loops over all groups/keys on EVERY iOS cold start, awaited before runApp
userSymptom: On iOS, users in many groups (or with many key generations) see a longer cold start; each launch serially re-writes every group key into the shared keychain before the UI can paint.
location: lib/main.dart:1297-1300 (both awaited, every launch); lib/features/groups/domain/repositories/group_repository_impl.dart:537-557 (mirrorAllKeysToSecureStore nested loop), :562-576 (mirrorAllMutedGroups loop)
evidence: main.dart:1297 `await groupRepository.mirrorAllKeysToSecureStore();` :1300 `await groupRepository.mirrorAllMutedGroups();`. mirrorAllKeysToSecureStore (group_repository_impl.dart:542-556): `for (final group in groups) { final keyRows = await dbLoadAllGroupKeys!(groupId); for (final row in keyRows) { final key = await _groupKeyFromRow(row); ... await _mirrorGroupKeyForPush(key); } }` — O(groups × keyGenerations) serial awaited DB reads + secure-storage writes. Guarded only by `pushSharedKeyStore == null` (:538) i.e. iOS-only; no per-launch 'already mirrored' sentinel, so it re-mirrors everything every launch.
rootCause: A self-healing keychain-projection backfill (for the iOS NSE) was placed unconditionally on the awaited pre-runApp path with no idempotency short-circuit, so it repeats full work each launch instead of only when something changed.
recommendation: Move both calls off the pre-frame path (unawaited / post-first-frame, alongside the deferred startLiveServices), and/or make them incremental: skip a group key whose shared-keychain entry already exists (containsKey check) and only mirror mute state when it differs. For the common case this collapses to a handful of containsKey reads or zero writes.

verdict.reasoning: Code matches the finding in the CURRENT tree. main.dart:1297/1300 await both mirror calls inside the unconditional main() bootstrap before runApp (main.dart:3090). HOT PATH confirmed for iOS: sharedPushKeyStore is non-null only on iOS (main.dart:424, `!kIsWeb && Platform.isIOS`), so the `pushSharedKeyStore == null` guards (group_repository_impl.dart:538, :563) make both no-ops on Android but full-work on every iOS cold start. TWO refinements lower the magnitude vs the discovery claim: (1) the KEYS path is NOT a full re-write each launch — _mirrorGroupKeyForPush (:663-665) early-returns when key.encryptedKey isSecureStoreReference, which is the normal steady-state storage shape (key material lives in the main keychain as a reference per _hydrateGroupKey :633-645), so the costly store.write at :668 fires only for legacy inline-plaintext rows; steady state is DB reads + one keychain READ per referenced row (_hydrateGroupKey :643) + cheap skips, few/zero writes. (2) the MUTES path has NO idempotency check — _mirrorGroupMutedForPush (:687-698) unconditionally write('1')/delete per group every launch, fully confirming that half. Cost: FlutterSecureKeyStore (flutter_secure_key_store.dart:30-31) does a real keychain op per call with first_unlock_this_device accessibility and a shared groupId access group; for a typical 10-30 group user this is tens of awaited keychain reads/writes + DB reads serially pre-frame — perceptible but tens of ms, not seconds. It is launch-only and does NOT touch the screen-to-screen navigation that dominates the user's hang report. Recommendation is sound and safe: move both off the awaited pre-frame path (unawaited/post-first-frame, like deferred startLiveServices at main.dart:3081) since they are self-healing backfills with no UI dependency; add a containsKey skip for mutes (SecureKeyStore.containsKey already exists, flutter_secure_key_store.dart:37); keys already partially short-circuit. Additionally make mirrorAllMutedGroups incremental: skip groups whose shared-keychain mute entry already matches (use the existing SecureKeyStore.containsKey at flutter_secure_key_store.dart:37) to collapse the common case to reads/zero writes. The keys loop already largely skips writes via the isSecureStoreReference early-return (group_repository_impl.dart:663), so prioritize the deferral over per-key change-detection there. A one-shot SharedPreferences/secure sentinel keyed on a schema/migration version would let both calls be skipped entirely after the first successful backfill.

title: Entire ~2200-line dependency graph is constructed synchronously on the root isolate before runApp, gating the first frame
userSymptom: Even with the awaited I/O removed, there is a fixed pre-frame CPU cost on every launch (constructing every repository, use case, listener and retrier inline) before any pixels are drawn — contributes to the 'not light' feel, worse on low-end Android.
location: lib/main.dart:439 (openEncryptedDatabase) through :3090 (runApp) — the whole body builds repositories (e.g. :1163 mediaAttachmentRepository, :1186 reactionRepository, postsRepository wiring :1080-1136), P2PServiceImpl (:2129), IncomingMessageRouter (:2239) and dozens of listeners/retriers (:2663-:3014) before runApp
evidence: `void main() async {` at :339; `runApp(` not reached until :3090 — ~2750 lines, all executed on the platform's main thread before the first frame is scheduled. P2PServiceImpl construction at :2129, message router at :2239, and the full retrier/listener set are all instantiated inline in main() rather than lazily. StartupTiming marks (run_app_called at :3192) confirm the team measures this gap.
rootCause: All DI is hand-rolled inline in main() (no DI container, no lazy providers), so every object the app could ever need is allocated before the first frame regardless of which screen the user lands on. Combined with the awaited I/O above, the splash cannot paint until construction completes.
recommendation: Reorder so a minimal shell (MaterialApp + StartupLoadingGate) is handed to runApp() as early as possible, then build the heavy graph behind the splash. Concretely: hoist runApp to right after the DB opens and identity repo is built, pass futures/late-initialized services into MyApp, and construct P2PServiceImpl + listeners + retriers inside the already-deferred startLiveServices()/post-frame callback. This pairs with finding #1 and turns the construction cost into post-first-frame work the user doesn't watch as a blank screen.

verdict.reasoning: Line numbers verified in current tree (lib/main.dart): void main at :339, P2PServiceImpl( at :2129, IncomingMessageRouter at :2239, runApp( at :3090, run_app_called StartupTiming mark at :3192 — file is 4620 lines. So the structural claim "the whole DI graph is hand-rolled inline in main() and fully allocated before runApp" is literally TRUE and runs on every cold launch (hot path). However the finding's CAUSAL claim — that the *construction/allocation* CPU cost gates the first frame and contributes to perceived jank — is largely refuted by reading the constructors. P2PServiceImpl (:2129-2212), IncomingMessageRouter (:2239), GroupInviteListener (:2683-2721), GroupKeyRepairRequestSender (:2668) etc. are all PLAIN Dart object constructors capturing closures and holding a `db`/repo reference; none do synchronous heavy work or I/O at construction. In AOT release, allocating a few hundred such objects is sub-millisecond-to-low-ms — not a perceptible blank-screen contributor. The genuinely expensive pre-frame work is the AWAITED I/O the finding explicitly hands off to "finding #1": await openEncryptedDatabase (:439, SQLCipher open + the long migration chain :443-459), await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory (:393), and critically `await startLiveServices()` at :3081 on the NON-share (normal) hot path, which runs await bridge.initialize() (Go node FFI bring-up, :3027), await notificationService.initialize() (:3029) and 20+ listener/retrier .start() calls (:3033-3064) BEFORE runApp. Note the team already proved the defer-behind-first-frame pattern works: deferredRuntimeStartup is wired (:3171 `isShareLaunch ? startLiveServices : null`) and _ensureRuntimeServicesReady (:3549-3567) defers it for share-launch only. The recommendation to defer the *.start()* set behind the first frame is sound and already-demonstrated; deferring *construction* yields near-zero benefit and is a large invasive refactor (MyApp's constructor at :3090-3190 takes ~60 pre-built references; P2PServiceImpl needs the replay-callback closures; listeners need messageRouter streams). Net: location accurate, hot-path true, but construction is not a meaningful jank source — the real cost lives in awaited startup, which this finding scopes out. Hence partial, severity lowered to low.
verdict.correctedLocation: lib/main.dart:3081 (await startLiveServices on the non-share hot path) and lib/main.dart:3027-3029 (await bridge.initialize / notificationService.initialize) are the real pre-frame cost; construction span :2129-3014 is cheap allocation. runApp at :3090.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Do NOT prioritize making object CONSTRUCTION lazy — in AOT release it is sub-ms allocation and the cross-wired graph (MyApp ctor takes ~60 references, P2PServiceImpl needs replay closures, listeners need router streams) makes lazy DI a large refactor for negligible CPU gain. Instead, extend the EXISTING deferred-startup machinery (deferredRuntimeStartup at :3171 / _ensureRuntimeServicesReady at :3549) to the normal launch path: stop awaiting startLiveServices() at :3081 before runApp, and instead pass `startLiveServices` as deferredRuntimeStartup unconditionally (not just isShareLaunch), running bridge.initialize()/notificationService.initialize()/listener+retrier .start() (:3026-3064) in a post-first-frame callback behind the StartupLoadingGate. That moves the actual perceptible blank-screen cost (Go FFI bring-up + 20+ .start()) off the pre-frame path. This overlaps with the separate awaited-I/O finding (DB open at :439); coordinate so the two are not landed as conflicting reorders.

title: Three awaited platform-channel probes run serially at the very top of main() before Firebase and the DB
userSymptom: A small, fixed serial latency at the start of every launch (share-intent probe, then Firebase, then docs-dir) before any other startup work begins.
location: lib/main.dart:348 (await shareIntentService.captureInitialIntent()), :389 (await ensureFirebaseReady), :393 (await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory())
evidence: main.dart:348 `final initialShareIntent = await shareIntentService.captureInitialIntent();` is the first awaited platform call on every launch (only consumed to set isShareLaunch). Then :389 awaits Firebase.initializeApp()+2 FCM setForegroundNotificationPresentationOptions/onBackgroundMessage calls, then :393 awaits getApplicationDocumentsDirectory(). These are sequential — each a MethodChannel round-trip — and Firebase init does not depend on the share probe.
rootCause: Independent platform-channel calls are awaited one after another instead of in parallel, and the share probe (rare path) is on the hot path for every launch.
recommendation: Kick off captureInitialIntent(), Firebase init, and getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() concurrently (start the futures, then await with Future.wait where ordering allows). getApplicationDocumentsDirectory and the share probe have no dependency on Firebase. This is a minor but free reduction of serial cold-start latency.

verdict.reasoning: Read lib/main.dart:339-413 and lib/core/services/share_intent_service.dart:55-67. The cited code exists and is on the cold-launch hot path: :348 `await shareIntentService.captureInitialIntent()` is the first awaited platform call (a real ReceiveSharingIntent.getInitialMedia round-trip per share_intent_service.dart:56), :393 `await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, and Firebase init in ensureFirebaseReady (:356-386). However the finding overstates a flat 3-call serial chain: the Firebase await at :388-389 is GATED on `if (!isShareLaunch)`, and on share launches Firebase is deferred entirely to startLiveServices (:3026, the deferredRuntimeStartup wiring at :3171). So only on the normal path are two probes (share + Firebase) serial before the DB; Firebase is not an unconditional third link. The result of captureInitialIntent is indeed only consumed to set isShareLaunch (:349), confirming the share probe is a rare-path call sitting on every launch's hot path. Magnitude is 2-3 MethodChannel round-trips (sub-ms to low-ms in release) — a fixed, negligible serial cost, NOT a cause of the reported screen-to-screen hangs/scroll stutter. The recommendation is only partially safe: share-probe and getApplicationDocumentsDirectory are genuinely independent and could overlap, but blanket Future.wait-ing Firebase with them would break the deliberate `if (!isShareLaunch)` deferral that keeps Firebase off the pre-DB critical path during share launches.
verdict.correctedLocation: lib/main.dart:348 (await captureInitialIntent), :388-389 (Firebase await gated on !isShareLaunch), :393 (await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory); Firebase deferral path at :3026/:3171; probe impl lib/core/services/share_intent_service.dart:55-67
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Only overlap the two truly independent probes: start shareIntentService.captureInitialIntent() and getApplicationDocumentsDirectory() as futures up front, then await both. Do NOT include ensureFirebaseReady() in a Future.wait — it is intentionally gated by `if (!isShareLaunch)` (:388) and deferred to startLiveServices (:3026) on share launches; parallelizing it would defeat that deferral. Net win is 1 MethodChannel round-trip (sub-ms to low-ms), so treat as a free micro-optimization, not a fix for the user's perceived jank — the real cold-start cost lives downstream (encrypted DB open, bridge.initialize, large synchronous DI wiring).

title: Default ambient background repaints the ENTIRE screen at 60fps on every screen (no RepaintBoundary isolating content)
userSymptom: Nothing ever feels 'light': constant low-grade stutter, scroll never glassy, transitions feel heavy, and battery drains — on every screen including the conversation, group, feed and orbit screens. Worse on older/cheaper Android devices from Google Play.
location: lib/features/identity/presentation/widgets/ambient_background.dart:123-196 (_DefaultAmbientBackground); used by all 17 screens via AmbientBackground (conversation_screen.dart:293, plus 16 others)
evidence: AmbientBackground is the DEFAULT (BackgroundPreference.defaultBackground) and runs _controller.repeat() with an 8s loop (ambient_background.dart:45-51). _DefaultAmbientBackground builds a Stack whose children are two AnimatedBuilder-driven Positioned glows AND the screen content `child` as a BARE third sibling (line 191: `child,`) — there is NO RepaintBoundary wrapping `child`. Each AnimatedBuilder rebuilds a Container+RadialGradient Decoration every frame (lines 139-189). Because the animating glows and the content share one paint layer in the same Stack with no boundary, every ambient frame marks the Stack subtree dirty and Flutter repaints the content too. This wraps all 17 screens (grep: 17 AmbientBackground call sites) so it is on the hot path for literally every screen the user sees.
rootCause: The animated glow layers and the static screen content are not separated by RepaintBoundaries, so the unavoidable 60fps glow animation forces a full-screen repaint each frame instead of repainting only the glow layers.
recommendation: Wrap the two glow AnimatedBuilders each in a RepaintBoundary AND wrap `child` in a RepaintBoundary (mirror what CosmicBackground already does at cosmic_background.dart:119/133). Better: lift the gradient Containers out of the AnimatedBuilder (they are constant — only the Positioned offset changes) by passing them via the AnimatedBuilder `child:` param and only animating the Positioned offsets, eliminating per-frame Decoration/shader allocation. Consider lowering the default-background motion to a slower/cheaper effect or honoring reduceMotion beyond just the feed surface.

location: lib/main.dart:3081 (await startLiveServices() before runApp at :3090); startLiveServices body lib/main.dart:3026 (await ensureFirebaseReady()), :3027 (await bridge.initialize()), :3029 (await notificationService.initialize()); plus earlier await ensureFirebaseReady() at :389
evidence: Line 3080-3082: `if (!isShareLaunch) { await startLiveServices(); }` runs BEFORE `runApp(` at 3090. startLiveServices awaits ensureFirebaseReady() (3026), bridge.initialize() (3027), notificationService.initialize() (3029) sequentially, then synchronously start()s ~25 listeners (3033-3064). ensureFirebaseReady is also awaited earlier at main.dart:389 and again at 3026. The actual P2P node:start is correctly DEFERRED (comment at 3056-3058: rejoinGroupTopics/drainGroupOfflineInbox happen in StartupRouter after node:start), so node start is not the blocker — but Firebase + notification channel init are bounded native round-trips on the critical pre-frame path.
rootCause: First frame is gated on non-UI-critical native initialization (Firebase, FCM token, notification channels) being fully awaited before runApp. None of this is required to paint the first screen.
recommendation: Move ensureFirebaseReady() and notificationService.initialize() off the pre-runApp critical path: call runApp() first (showing a splash/startup router), then kick off these initializations via unawaited()/post-first-frame (WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback) and let the StartupRouter/feed react when they complete. Keep only the bare minimum (documents dir, DB open, identity read) before runApp. De-duplicate the double ensureFirebaseReady() await (389 + 3026).

First Firebase await at :389. FlutterNotificationService.initialize body: lib/core/notifications/flutter_notification_service.dart:23-53. GoBridgeClient.initialize body: lib/core/bridge/go_bridge_client.dart:158-184.
verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED the structural claim: main() (main.dart:339) serially awaits ensureFirebaseReady() at :389 and then startLiveServices() at :3081 BEFORE runApp() at :3090. startLiveServices (defined :3017) awaits ensureFirebaseReady() (:3026), bridge.initialize() (:3027), notificationService.initialize() (:3029), then synchronously start()s ~25 listeners (:3033-3064). So the first interactive frame IS gated on pre-runApp native init — true, and this runs on EVERY cold launch (hot path for launch).

But several cost claims are OVERSTATED, hence partial not confirmed:
1. The 'double ensureFirebaseReady await' is effectively FREE. The body (main.dart:356-360) latches on firebaseInitialized=true; the call at :3026 returns immediately. Firebase.initializeApp() (line 363) runs exactly ONCE, via the :389 call. De-duping is cosmetic, not a perf win.
2. bridge.initialize() is NOT a bounded native round-trip. GoBridgeClient.initialize() (go_bridge_client.dart:158-184) only subscribes to an EventChannel broadcast stream (_eventChannel.receiveBroadcastStream().listen) and emits flow events — no awaited platform call, near-zero cost. The finding correctly omits it from the cost list, but it sits on the awaited chain regardless.
3. The genuinely frame-gating native cost is: one Firebase.initializeApp() (main.dart:363) + notificationService.initialize() which does await _plugin.initialize(), await ensureMknoonNotificationChannel(), await getNotificationAppLaunchDetails() (flutter_notification_service.dart:39-46) — 3 platform-channel calls, plus on iOS requestApplePermissions:true (line 29-31) can surface the APNs prompt. That is real but bounded, and ONLY on cold launch — not every navigation/frame/scroll.
4. The finding correctly acknowledges node:start IS deferred — verified by the comment at main.dart:3056-3058 and deferredRuntimeStartup plumbing (:3171, _ensureRuntimeServicesReady :3549-3567). So the heavy P2P startup is already off the pre-frame path.

Net: real but modest cold-launch-only delay, not the screen-to-screen hang / scroll stutter the user mainly reports. Severity medium is generous; low is more accurate.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Sound in direction but apply with care. (a) DROP the 'de-duplicate double await' item — it is already latched (main.dart:357-359) and costs nothing. (b) The safe win is to call runApp() with a splash/StartupRouter FIRST, then run ensureFirebaseReady() + notificationService.initialize() via addPostFrameCallback/unawaited and have StartupRouter await a readiness Future before routing — mirrors the existing deferredRuntimeStartup pattern already used for the share-launch path (main.dart:3171, :3549-3567), so the codebase already has the plumbing. (c) HAZARD: notificationService.initialize() calls getNotificationAppLaunchDetails() and sets up onNotificationTap; cold notif-tap routing (consumeInitialPayload at flutter_notification_service.dart:76) depends on this being ready before StartupRouter routes — deferring it must keep the initial-payload consumption ordered, or cold notification-tap launches regress. (d) Keep documents dir / DB open / identity read before runApp (they feed the first routing decision). Measure with the existing StartupTiming marks (firebase_ready, notification_service_ready, runtime_services_ready) before/after to confirm the gain is worth the routing-order risk.

title: RingAvatar regenerates its deterministic avatar model (hash + Fisher-Yates shuffle + ring params) in build() for every photoless avatar, with no memoization
userSymptom: Minor scroll stutter in lists with many photoless contacts (feed, orbit, contact pickers) and extra GC churn; contributes to the app not feeling 'light' but is not a primary hitch by itself.
location: lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/ring_avatar.dart:32-44 (build → RingAvatarGenerator.generate(peerId, size) every build); generator lib/core/utils/ring_avatar_generator.dart:64-86; UserAvatar falls back to RingAvatar at lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/user_avatar.dart:156,162,218
evidence: RingAvatar.build() line 34: `final data = RingAvatarGenerator.generate(peerId, size);` runs unconditionally per build. generate() (generator.dart:64) does djb2Hash over the peerId string, _shuffleColors (Fisher-Yates loop), a per-ring loop building _RingParams, _calculateRingRadii, and _generateGlow — allocating fresh objects each time. RingAvatar is the priority-2/3 fallback for every UserAvatar without a photo (user_avatar.dart:156,162) and is used across feed/orbit/conversation/contacts. The painter itself is correct (ring_avatar_painter.dart:106 has a real shouldRepaint), so the waste is purely the per-build model recompute + allocation, not raster.
rootCause: Deterministic, input-stable data (depends only on peerId+size) is recomputed every build instead of being cached. For a list with many rows this multiplies a small constant cost by visible-row count on every frame the list rebuilds.
recommendation: Memoize RingAvatarGenerator.generate with a small static LRU/Map cache keyed on (peerId, size) (the output is deterministic and immutable), or compute it once in a StatefulWidget/didUpdateWidget instead of build(). This removes the hash+shuffle+allocation from the per-frame path for free.

(165-196), and _generateGlow with an HSL→Color conversion (225-243) — allocating ~9 fresh objects (4 RingData + 4 _RingParams + 1 GlowData + 1 RingAvatarData + a palette List copy) every build. HOT PATH confirmed: RingAvatar is the photoless fallback at user_avatar.dart:156, 162, and 218 (read lines 130-225); UserAvatar( appears in 34 lib files including scroll-list rows letter_card_one_to_one.dart, letter_card_group.dart, friend_row.dart, group_member_row.dart, contact_picker_row.dart, and the multi-avatar orbit/orbit2/orbit3 visualizations; FeedRingAvatar (feed_ring_avatar.dart:25) and share_target_picker_screen.dart:439 wrap RingAvatar directly. ADDITIONAL DEFECT the discovery agent UNDER-stated: it claimed 'the waste is purely the model recompute, not raster.' That is too lenient — RingData/GlowData/RingAvatarData (generator.dart:5-51) have NO operator==/hashCode (grep confirms only the three class declarations, zero == overrides), so ring_avatar_painter.dart:108 `oldDelegate.data != data` is ALWAYS true because each build mints a fresh-identity RingAvatarData → the CustomPaint also re-RASTERS on every rebuild of the widget, not just recomputes the model. Both are READ-stable, low-risk refactors with no behavioral change.

(2) Add value-based operator==/hashCode to RingAvatarData, RingData, and GlowData (or rely on memoization giving identity-stable instances) so RingAvatarPainter.shouldRepaint (ring_avatar_painter.dart:108) stops always returning true — currently the fresh-identity RingAvatarData forces an unnecessary re-RASTER on every rebuild, which the discovery agent missed. Together this drops both the model recompute and the redundant raster off the per-frame/scroll path for photoless avatars at zero behavioral cost.

title: UserAvatar Image.memory decodes full-resolution avatar bytes with no cacheWidth/cacheHeight for a small (~42px) target
userSymptom: Higher memory footprint and occasional decode hitch when the user's own avatar first appears; contributes to the app feeling heavy on memory-constrained devices, but decode is off the UI isolate so it is not a direct frame stall.
location: lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/user_avatar.dart:119-126
evidence: Image.memory(avatarBytes!, key: ValueKey(avatarBytes.hashCode), fit: BoxFit.cover, width: size, height: size, errorBuilder: _errorBuilder) — no cacheWidth/cacheHeight. The image is decoded at full source resolution then downscaled to `size` (default 42). Note Uint8List.hashCode is identity-based so the ValueKey is cheap (not a hashing cost). Decode happens off-isolate in the engine, so this is a memory/GPU-upload cost, not a UI-isolate block.
rootCause: No decode-size hint, so a potentially large JPEG is decoded to a multi-hundred-px bitmap for a 42px circle, wasting image-cache memory.
recommendation: Pass cacheWidth/cacheHeight (e.g. (size * devicePixelRatio).round()) to Image.memory (and the Image.file branch at :144) so the engine decodes at display resolution. Out-of-dimension for main-isolate blocking but a cheap 'feels lighter' memory win.

So the wasted decode is ~512x512x4 ≈ 1 MB ARGB cached for a 42px (~126px @3x) target — a real ~15x memory overdraw, fixed ~1 MB per widget, single avatar per screen (not per-row/per-scroll). title: AmbientBackground runs a never-stopping repeat() animation on ~16 screens, repainting two radial-gradient glows every frame
userSymptom: App never feels 'light' or idle; constant low-grade GPU/CPU draw and battery drain; subtle continuous shimmer/micro-stutter that makes scrolls and screen transitions feel less smooth because the raster thread never gets to rest.
location: lib/features/identity/presentation/widgets/ambient_background.dart:45-52 (controller + repeat), :139-189 (two AnimatedBuilder glows); used by 16 screens incl. lib/features/conversation/presentation/screens/conversation_screen.dart, lib/features/groups/presentation/screens/group_conversation_screen.dart, lib/features/feed/presentation/screens/feed_screen.dart:185, lib/features/orbit/presentation/screens/orbit_screen.dart:329
evidence: initState: `_controller = AnimationController(vsync:this, duration: const Duration(seconds:8)); if (_shouldAnimate) _controller.repeat();` — `_shouldAnimate` is true for the DEFAULT background on every surface except the feed under reduceMotion. The _DefaultAmbientBackground builds two `AnimatedBuilder(animation: animation, builder: ...)` that on every tick rebuild a `Container(decoration: BoxDecoration(shape: circle, gradient: RadialGradient(...)))` of 300x300 and 350x350 px. Grep confirms 17 AmbientBackground call sites (16 screens). The animation never stops while the screen is mounted.
rootCause: A purely decorative ambient glow uses an infinite `repeat()` controller. Because the controller drives AnimatedBuilders that allocate a new BoxDecoration/RadialGradient and re-composite two large translucent circles every frame, the engine is forced to produce a new frame ~continuously on every screen (chat, orbit, group, settings) for the whole foreground session. reduceMotion only gates the feed surface (isFeedSurface && reduceMotion); all other 15 callers animate unconditionally.
recommendation: 1) Honor reduceMotion / MediaQuery.disableAnimations on ALL surfaces, not just the feed, and render the static value==0 frame when reduced. 2) Drop the animation duration cost: either slow it dramatically (e.g. 30-40s) or, better, stop the controller after settling and only animate on entrance, since the motion is barely perceptible. 3) Hoist the gradient out of the per-frame builder — precompute the two BoxDecorations once (they are constant; only the Offset changes) and animate only the Positioned top/left/bottom/right via the builder so Flutter doesn't reallocate gradients each tick. 4) Consider RepaintBoundary around each glow so the moving glow does not invalidate the whole subtree's raster. Highest leverage: gate the repeat() behind reduced-motion everywhere and stop it when not needed.

verdict.refinedRecommendation: Highest leverage: gate _controller.repeat() behind reduced-motion (MediaQuery.disableAnimations || accessibleNavigation) on ALL surfaces, not just isFeedSurface — read it in didChangeDependencies and feed it into _shouldAnimate so every default-background screen renders the static value==0 frame under reduced motion (the feed already does this at feed_screen.dart:141; just generalize it inside the widget). Then make the motion cheaper regardless of preference: (a) pull the two BoxDecoration/RadialGradient objects out of the per-tick builder into final const-ish fields so the AnimatedBuilder only updates the Positioned top/left/bottom/right offsets (the gradients never change — only the sin/cos offset does), and (b) wrap each glow in a RepaintBoundary so the moving translucent circles do not invalidate the sibling screen-content layer on the raster thread. Optionally lengthen the 8s loop to ~30s; the motion is barely perceptible. Existing didUpdateWidget already has a clean start/stop path, so adding a reduced-motion stop is low-risk.
verdict.reasoning: Read the current source directly. ambient_background.dart:45-52 confirms `_controller = AnimationController(vsync:this, duration: const Duration(seconds:8))` then `if (_shouldAnimate) _controller.repeat();` — an infinite vsync-rate loop. `_shouldAnimate` (lines 116-120) returns true for any caller when preference==defaultBackground, gating OFF only when `isFeedSurface && reduceMotion`. grep of lib shows 16 call sites; only feed_screen.dart:185-190 passes isFeedSurface/reduceMotion, the other 15 (conversation_screen.dart:293, group_conversation_screen.dart:194, orbit_screen.dart:329, settings_screen.dart:96, group_list_screen.dart:82, qr_display_screen.dart:105, etc.) use the defaults so they animate unconditionally. background_preference.dart:39 confirms defaultBackground is the fallback for null/unknown, so a fresh-install user who never changes the setting hits the animated _DefaultAmbientBackground on every non-feed screen — genuine hot path (every navigation, whole foreground session). The two AnimatedBuilders at :139-189 reallocate Positioned→Container→BoxDecoration→RadialGradient every tick, do NOT use AnimatedBuilder's child cache, and have no RepaintBoundary, so the raster thread repaints two translucent gradients every vsync and never idles. Refinement vs the finding: the Dart rebuild is bounded to the two small builder subtrees (widget.child is a Stack sibling at :191, NOT inside the builders), so it is not a whole-screen rebuild storm — the dominant cost is the continuous raster repaint + engine never idling, which degrades scroll/transition headroom and battery rather than causing the discrete screen-to-screen HANGS the user reports (those are blocking-work bugs elsewhere). Hence medium, not high. Recommendation is sound and safe; the widget already has a didUpdateWidget start/stop path to build on. The 145/146/147 notif-tap work did not touch this file.

title: Conversation/group chat: every incoming message, status change, and reaction does an un-coalesced whole-screen setState that re-runs an O(N) display-grouping pass — a relay-drain burst becomes O(M*N) full rebuilds
userSymptom: Opening a chat from a notification (or after backgrounding) stutters/hangs briefly while drained messages 'pop in' one by one; reactions arriving in a burst cause visible jank. This is the 'feels buggy after notif-tap' symptom — the screen opens fast but then hitches as the relay drain replays.
location: lib/features/conversation/presentation/screens/conversation_wired.dart:1509-1548 (per-message repo-change setState), :1481-1499 (incoming), :3352-3375 (per-reaction whole-screen setState); message_repository_impl.dart:121-141 (one messageChanges event PER saveMessage); list recompute at lib/features/conversation/presentation/screens/conversation_screen.dart:446-447 + 684-771 (_buildDisplayItems). Mirror in lib/features/groups/presentation/screens/group_conversation_wired.dart:1409-1480 + group_conversation_screen.dart:559-571,774-820
evidence: saveMessage emits per message: `_messageChangeController.add(saved);` (message_repository_impl.dart:141). The screen subscribes `changeSource.messageChanges.where(...).listen((message) async { ... setState(() { _upsertMessageById(...); }); })` with NO debounce/batch. Each setState rebuilds ConversationScreen, whose build calls `_buildMessageList()` → `_buildDisplayItems()` which loops over ALL widget.messages twice (run-grouping forward pass `for (var i=0;i<widget.messages.length;i++)` with `DateTime.tryParse(message.timestamp)` + `_formatDateLabel` per message, then a second forward pass for last-in-run). _onIncomingReactionChange (3352) also does a full setState. During a relay drain of M messages each save fires one event → M setStates × O(N) display recompute.
rootCause: No batching layer between the per-row repository change stream and the UI: the repo emits one event per persisted row, and the screen turns each into an independent whole-screen setState. The list-item model (_DisplayItems with run-grouping) is recomputed from scratch on every one of those rebuilds rather than incrementally or memoized, so the cost scales with conversation length on each of the burst events.
recommendation: Coalesce the burst: buffer messageChanges with a microtask/short timer (e.g. `Stream.transform` with a 16-32ms debounce, or accumulate into a pending set and flush once per frame via SchedulerBinding.addPostFrameCallback) so a drain of M rows triggers ONE setState. Separately, memoize _buildDisplayItems: cache the computed List<_DisplayItem> keyed by the messages list identity (and reactions identity) so it only recomputes when the underlying list actually changes, and/or move grouping/date-label computation into the data layer (compute once when a message is appended). Cache parsed timestamps on ConversationMessage instead of DateTime.tryParse on every build. The await _resolveHydratedMediaForMessage inside the listener (1529) also serializes the burst — that media hydration should not gate the text upsert.

title: Database opened without WAL journal mode + 5s busy_timeout — UI reads can block up to 5s behind inbox-drain writes (perceived hang)
userSymptom: Occasional multi-second hangs when navigating right after a push/notification or when messages are syncing — taps register late or the screen freezes, then unsticks.
location: lib/core/database/encrypted_db_opener.dart:82-101 (openDatabase onConfigure sets only PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000; no journal_mode/WAL, no synchronous tuning)
evidence: onConfigure runs only `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`. There is no `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`. In default rollback-journal mode, a writer takes an exclusive lock that blocks concurrent readers; with the 5s busy_timeout a UI-isolate read issued during an inbox drain / replay commit loop will wait (up to 5s) for the writer rather than reading a stable snapshot. Recent drain de-blocking (145/146/147) reduced await chains but the writes still serialize against UI reads at the SQLite level.
rootCause: Rollback-journal mode serializes readers against the active writer; the drain/replay path does many sequential writes, so a navigation-triggered read can queue behind them for the full busy_timeout window.
recommendation: In onConfigure add `await db.rawQuery('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL');` (and consider `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;`). WAL lets readers proceed against a snapshot while a write is in progress, eliminating reader-vs-writer stalls during drain. Validate WAL is supported with SQLCipher on the target platforms; it is the standard recommendation. Keep busy_timeout as a safety net.

It is genuinely hot-path: main.dart:439 opens the single app DB (identity.db) at launch, and every repository read on every navigation/scroll uses that one Database. So the config gap and hot-path are confirmed. BUT the finding's causal mechanism is refuted. It claims a UI read issued during a drain "waits up to 5s for the writer in rollback-journal mode." That requires concurrent connections contending at SQLite's file-lock layer. This app uses sqflite_sqlcipher → sqflite's single serialized native connection. In sqflite_common-2.5.6/lib/src/database_mixin.dart, reads (txnRawQuery, lines 672-677, reached via rawQuery line 148) AND writes (txnExecute, line 610) BOTH route through txnSynchronized → the same `_rawLock.synchronized` (line 573). All ops already serialize behind ONE Dart-level FIFO mutex on a single connection. A read issued mid-drain is never dispatched to native SQLite until the in-flight write op releases _rawLock — it never reaches the rollback-journal reader-vs-writer exclusive lock that busy_timeout guards. The busy_timeout's actual purpose (per the code comment, lines 87-92) is a stale/external lock-holder on open, not the app's own reads. Therefore WAL would NOT eliminate the described symptom: any stall is Dart-mutex queueing behind a long write batch plus per-query SQLCipher crypto cost, neither of which WAL addresses (WAL grants no Dart-layer concurrency with one connection). The recommendation is largely a no-op for the claimed multi-second hang; WAL+synchronous=NORMAL offers only a smaller write-commit fsync reduction and carries unvalidated SQLCipher/iOS file-coordination caveats. Severity lowered to low: real-but-cosmetic config gap, wrong diagnosis, no perceptible-hang fix.

title: Every chat message bubble wraps itself in a sigma-24 BackdropFilter (Gaussian blur) — 8-12 saveLayer+blur passes per scroll frame on the GPU raster thread, on BOTH 1:1 and group chats
userSymptom: Scrolling a conversation stutters / drops frames and the chat 'never feels light'; the heavier the scrollback, the worse it feels. Distinct from a UI-thread hang — the UI thread can be idle while the raster thread misses its 16ms budget.
location: lib/features/conversation/presentation/widgets/letter_card.dart:196-199 (_buildBubble path, ClipRRect+BackdropFilter sigma 24) and :712-715 (avatar-outside/group bubble, same blur); selected as the default render path at :190-191 (if (bubbleLayout) return _buildBubble); enabled by callers lib/features/conversation/presentation/screens/conversation_screen.dart:585 (bubbleLayout: true) and lib/features/groups/presentation/screens/group_conversation_screen.dart:665 (bubbleLayout: true)
evidence: letter_card.dart:712 `final bubble = ClipRRect(borderRadius: radius, child: BackdropFilter(filter: ImageFilter.blur(sigmaX: 24, sigmaY: 24), child: Container(...)))` — this is the bubble for EVERY message row. conversation_screen.dart:585 and group_conversation_screen.dart:665 both build LetterCard with `bubbleLayout: true`, and LetterCard.build at :190 routes bubbleLayout→_buildBubble. ListView.builder gives each row a RepaintBoundary so they don't repaint on the ambient tick, but during scroll EACH visible bubble still re-executes its own BackdropFilter (a saveLayer + Gaussian blur that samples the layer behind it). With ~8-12 bubbles visible that is 8-12 blur passes per scroll frame.
rootCause: BackdropFilter is one of the most expensive Flutter primitives: it forces a saveLayer of the backdrop region and runs a two-pass Gaussian blur on the GPU. Applying it per message bubble multiplies that cost by the number of visible rows on every scroll frame. A blur of the background behind an opaque-ish surface is visually near-identical to a flat translucent fill, so the cost buys almost nothing perceptible behind text bubbles.
recommendation: Drop the per-bubble BackdropFilter. Replace the ClipRRect+BackdropFilter+Container with a plain Container/DecoratedBox using a semi-opaque solid color (readableColors.surfaceRaised/surfaceSubtle already provide the tint) — no saveLayer, no blur. If a frosted look is required, render ONE backdrop blur for the whole list region behind the ListView (not per row), or use a pre-baked translucent color. Same change in both letter_card.dart blur sites (:198, :714). This removes O(visible-rows) GPU blur passes per scroll frame.

title: First open of a chat compiles the blur (BackdropFilter) shader pipeline on the raster thread → a one-time stutter/hang on the first conversation opened per session
userSymptom: The FIRST time you open a chat (or the feed) after launch there is a brief freeze/jank as the screen appears; subsequent opens are smoother. Reads as 'opening a screen hangs the first time.'
location: lib/features/conversation/presentation/widgets/letter_card.dart:199/715 + conversation_header.dart:36 + compose_area.dart:314 + feed_navigation_bar.dart:34 (all ImageFilter.blur, first appear on first chat/feed mount); no shader-warmup / SkSL bundle or precompile step found (grep of lib for precacheImage/shader warm-up returns nothing relevant; pubspec has no bundled SkSL)
evidence: The app introduces BackdropFilter blur pipelines that are only exercised the first time a screen containing them is rasterized. On a release build the engine (Impeller on iOS, and Skia/Impeller on Android) must compile/prepare the blur pipeline on first use, which lands on the raster thread and shows as a single dropped-frame cluster the first time a chat or the feed is shown. There is no warm-up in main.dart and no bundled shader cache, so it happens on the user's first navigation each cold session.
rootCause: Flutter compiles GPU shader/pipeline state lazily on first use; blur is a non-trivial pipeline. Without a warm-up frame or precompiled cache, the cost is paid in front of the user on the first screen that uses it.
recommendation: Lowest-risk: reduce reliance on BackdropFilter per finding #1/#2 (fewer/no blur pipelines to compile). If blur is kept, render one off-screen warm-up frame containing a BackdropFilter during the splash/startup (after runApp, post-first-frame) so the pipeline is compiled before the first real chat open. On iOS verify Impeller is enabled (it precompiles a fixed pipeline set and largely eliminates this), and avoid the legacy SkSL path. Note: this is a one-time-per-session stutter, lower priority than the steady-state per-frame blur cost.

No precacheImage / shader warmup in lib/ and no SkSL bundle in pubspec.yaml — confirmed via grep. So the static facts hold, and blur is genuinely on the hot chat-render path (with a location correction: the DEFAULT path is bubbleLayout:true — conversation_screen.dart:585 passes bubbleLayout:true; build() returns at letter_card.dart:190-191 before reaching the cited :199 legacy branch, then hits the blur at :715. Line 199 is the bubbleLayout:false legacy path, NOT the hot one). However, the finding's CAUSAL MECHANISM is refuted. `flutter --version` reports Flutter 3.41.4 stable / Dart SDK 3.9.0 / engine e4b8dca3f1 (2026-03). On this version Impeller is the default+sole renderer on iOS and the default on Android, and there is NO FLTDisableImpeller key in ios/Runner/Info.plist (grep returned none) and no Impeller-disable meta-data in android AndroidManifest.xml. Impeller ships precompiled pipelines built at engine-compile time precisely to eliminate the runtime first-use shader/pipeline compilation jank that the legacy Skia/SkSL path suffered. The finding's premise ('the engine must compile/prepare the blur pipeline on first use, which lands on the raster thread … happens on the first navigation each cold session') is the legacy SkSL behavior Impeller removed — the finding itself concedes 'On iOS verify Impeller is enabled (it precompiles a fixed pipeline set and largely eliminates this).' Since Impeller is active here, the one-time first-open shader-COMPILE hang it describes does not occur on iOS and is largely mitigated on Android. The steady-state per-frame BackdropFilter raster cost is a real and separate concern (covered by findings #1/#2), but that is NOT the one-time-first-use compile stutter asserted here. The proposed off-screen warm-up frame fix is therefore solving a non-problem on this build and adds startup work for no benefit.
